request: Hi , Please create an outlet port on the top right and an inlet port on the bottom left .

parameters.port_style: hose_nipple/boss + internal through-hole into header tank
parameters.sizing_strategy: match existing side-port geometry already present on the opposite end of the top header tank (mirror/clone)
parameters.edge_treatment: TBD (match existing: small lead-in chamfer or fillet on port mouth)
parameters.placement_strategy: mirror of existing top-end side port across radiator long mid-plane (Y=0) to the opposite end; keep same offset from top edge and same lateral offset from corner radii

actions.target: Top header tank, right end (top-right of assembly when viewing the fan/guard side as in the provided 'right' view); create a new outlet port that mirrors the existing top-left end side port visible in the multiview images.
actions.relational_constraint: Port located on the top header tank (SEC02) at the opposite end from the existing hose connectors (SEC09); position at the right end of the radiator (opposite side of the existing top-side port) while maintaining equivalent edge offsets; axis normal to the end face of the header/end-tank region.
actions.unresolved_reference: Exact port specification is not provided: (1) standard/type (barb, NPT/BSPP threaded, quick-connect), (2) exact OD/ID/length, (3) whether port should include thread/counterbore, (4) which global direction defines 'right' if model orientation is different. If the intention is to duplicate the existing top-side port, mirroring will preserve geometry and resolve sizing. Also, model.json does not explicitly list a face_code for the end-tank side face where the existing top-side port sits; end-face selection may require picking the end planar face in CAD.
steps: Context/intent check (functional): because this is an outlet port and should connect to the top header volume, place it on the TopHeaderTankAndFiller (SEC02), not on the core fin field (SEC01) or fan/guard parts (SEC04-SEC07). Ensure it does not intersect guards/fans and maintains clearance to mounting bosses (SEC08).

Identify the radiator long mid-plane used for left/right mirroring: create/use a datum mid-plane centered between the two ends of the radiator (typically the plane that bisects the core length; use symmetry note—layout is approximately symmetric along the long direction). If a default origin plane represents this, reuse it; otherwise create a construction plane halfway between the two end faces.

Localize the ‘right end’ reference: use the core/frame end plane on the right side as the placement reference. In model.json, the best available proxy for the end boundary is Core_side_end_plane_posY (face_code 0002, Brep FACE 1). Confirm in CAD that this plane corresponds to the right-side end face in the multiview images (opposite the end that already carries the brass hose connectors).

Create/obtain the end-face sketch plane: select the planar end face of the top header/end-tank region coincident with the right end (if the end-tank has its own planar face, prefer that; otherwise use a datum plane coincident/offset to face_code 0002). Set sketch normal pointing outward from the radiator body.

Geometry reuse strategy (preferred for fidelity): select the existing top-end side port feature on the opposite end (top-left port visible in images) by selecting its cylindrical outer face and adjacent blend faces; perform a feature/body Mirror across the long mid-plane (Y=0) to create a symmetric duplicate on the right end. Join/boolean-union the mirrored boss into the top header tank solid.

If mirroring the existing feature is not feasible (feature not separable): manually recreate the port. On the right-end sketch plane, sketch a circle for the port boss OD located by mirroring the existing port center: constrain the center point by equal offsets from the top edge of the top header tank (refer to Top_tank_outer_plane face_code 0007 / FACE 24 for top boundary) and from the end-tank corner radius/side edge; then fully define with dimensions equal to the left-side port’s measured offsets.
Extrude (add) the boss: Extrude the boss profile outward (away from the tank) to the same length as the existing top-side port projection; operation = Add/Join to the top header tank body.

Create the internal flow passage: on the boss end face, sketch the port ID circle concentric with the boss; Extrude-Cut (or Hole feature) inward to break through into the top header tank cavity. Use ‘Up to Next/Up to Face’ targeting the internal wall as appropriate to avoid cutting through unintended regions.

Edge finishing: apply a small chamfer or fillet at the port mouth and at the boss-to-tank junction to match the style of existing fittings; keep consistent blend radii for stress reduction and hose insertion.

Interference/clearance check: verify no clash with fan guards (SEC06/SEC07), and ensure adequate wall thickness around the penetration into the header tank. Validate that the new outlet port is on the top-right in the fan-side ('right' view) orientation.

steps: Context/intent check (functional): because this is an inlet port feeding the bottom header volume, place it on BottomHeaderTankAndDrainRegion (SEC03). Do not place it on the heat-exchanger fin face (SEC01) where it would compromise the matrix and airflow path.
Establish the same long-direction mid-plane (Y=0) used for mirroring the top port so that the inlet port is a symmetric counterpart of the existing bottom-side end port.

Localize the ‘left end’ reference: use the core/frame end plane on the left side as the placement reference. In model.json, the best available proxy is Core_side_end_plane_negY (face_code 0003, Brep FACE 3). Confirm in CAD that this corresponds to the left end as seen in the multiview images (the end showing the brass hose connectors in the 'right' view).

Create/obtain the end-face sketch plane: select the planar end face of the bottom header/end-tank region coincident with the left end (or create a datum plane coincident to face_code 0003). Ensure sketch normal points outward from the radiator body.

Geometry reuse strategy (preferred): select the existing bottom-end side port on the opposite end (bottom-right port visible in images) by selecting its cylindrical outer face and adjacent blends; Mirror the feature/body across the long mid-plane (Y=0) to create the symmetric duplicate on the left end. Boolean-union the mirrored boss into the bottom header tank solid.

If mirroring the existing feature is not feasible: manually recreate. On the left-end sketch plane, sketch the boss OD circle and place its center by mirroring the existing bottom-side port’s center location: constrain offsets from the bottom edge using Bottom_tank_outer_plane (face_code 0009 / FACE 42) as the bottom boundary reference, and constrain lateral offsets from the corner/side edge to match the existing port.
Extrude (add) the boss outward to match the existing bottom-side port length; Join to the bottom header tank.

Create the internal inlet passage: sketch concentric ID circle on the boss end face; perform Extrude-Cut/Hole inward to break through into the bottom header tank cavity, using Up-to-Next/Up-to-Face termination to avoid unintended through-cuts.
Edge finishing: apply chamfer/fillet at the port mouth and boss root to match the existing port styling and reduce stress concentration.

Connectivity/clearance check: confirm this new inlet port is bottom-left in the fan-side ('right' view) orientation and does not interfere with nearby fittings or mounting features; verify sufficient wall thickness around the penetration.

intention: Add connection points for fluid/flow: one functioning as an outlet and one functioning as an inlet.
Maintain design consistency by duplicating/mirroring existing side port geometry so the new ports match established manufacturing style, wall thickness, and hose-interface behavior.

Place ports on the appropriate header tanks (top for outlet, bottom for inlet) to support intended coolant routing while avoiding interference with fan/guard assemblies and preserving heat-exchanger core integrity.
